approaches.name: Palmar / volar modified Henry (FCR)
selection_indications: Common for volar plating; definitive selection follows fracture morphology and planned fixation.
selection_limitations: A more ulnar palmar exposure may be chosen when direct median nerve exposure is required.
Dorsal fragments may require a dorsal or combined strategy.
positioning: Supine with the arm on a radiolucent hand table and fluoroscopic access.
exposure: Develop the FCR-based volar interval, mobilize the flexor pollicis longus, and elevate pronator quadratus to expose the distal radius.

structures_at_risk.structure: Palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve
structures_at_risk.protection: Avoid blind ulnar dissection around the FCR sheath.
Respect the watershed line and restore soft-tissue coverage when possible.

pitfalls: Plate prominence distal to the watershed line
questions: Q: Why does the watershed line matter? A: Excessively distal volar plate prominence can irritate or injure the flexor tendons.
Q: What must be checked after fixation besides the radiocarpal reduction? A: Confirm screw containment and assess DRUJ motion and stability.
approaches.coverage_notes: Technique is fracture-pattern dependent; this module does not imply that every distal radius fracture should receive a volar plate.

approaches.name: Dorsal distal forearm
selection_indications: Consider when the fracture pattern or fixation strategy requires direct dorsal/intermediate or radial-column access.
selection_limitations: Extensor tendon handling and implant prominence are central limitations; the exact interval is chosen by the fragment pattern.
positioning: Supine on a hand table with the forearm positioned for dorsal access and biplanar imaging.
exposure: Use the required interval between extensor compartments; a third-compartment approach mobilizes EPL and permits subperiosteal elevation of the fourth compartment for intermediate-column exposure.

structures_at_risk.protection: Identify, mobilize, and ensure a low-friction final course.

structures_at_risk.risk_phase: Radial skin flap and radial-column exposure
structures_at_risk.protection: Identify and protect the sensory branch in the radial flap.

pitfalls: Injuring EPL while opening the third compartment
Leaving a tendon directly over prominent dorsal hardware without protective retinacular management
questions: Q: Which landmark identifies the EPL compartment? A: EPL turns around Lister's tubercle in the third extensor compartment.
Q: Why can a dorsal approach be selected? A: It provides direct access to dorsal/intermediate or radial-column fragments when dictated by the fracture pattern.
approaches.coverage_notes: Dorsal intervals are fragment-specific; this summarizes the common third-compartment/intermediate-column exposure.
